To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NO produced by endothelial cells coordinates the propagation of Ca2+ waves and the frequency of Ca oscillations in hepatocytes in the intact liver.
bradykinin, acting via endothelial-derived nitroso-compounds, sensitizes the hepatocyte to vasopressin-induced Ca2+ signalling.

bradykinin stimulates the release of NO from endothelial cells, and that this NO acts on the hepatocytes to increase the frequency of Ca(2+) oscillations and the amplitude of intercellular Ca(2+) waves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms by which the liver responds to changes in blood flow and oxygenation.
the coordination of calcium signalling in the intact liver and in isolated hepatocytes, and with the role of nitric oxide in these processes.
the coordination of calcium signaling by endothelial-derived Nitric Oxide in the intact liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endothelium of the hepatic microvasculature plays a pivotal role in the propagation of vasodilatory Ca2+ waves and in the coordination of the frequency of hepatocyte Ca2+ oscillation.
the NO/cGMP pathway has an inhibitory effect on the propagation of vasovagal Ca2+ signals across hepatic plates and the frequency of hepatocellular Ca2+ signals in the intact liver.

the endothelial-derived nitro-vasodilator, bradykinin, modulates hepatic calcium oscillations via NO, which in turn, coordinates the propagation of intercellular Ca(2+) waves across hepatic lobules in the intact liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO is a key regulator of Ca2+ signalling in the intact liver and that endothelial cells are the main source for NO in the intact liver.
endothelial-derived nitrite oxide (NO) is an important regulator of Ca2+ signalling in liver, and that NO may coordinate Ca2+ signalling across the liver lobule.
the endothelial cell is a key player in the coordination of Ca2+ signalling between different cell types in the intact liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coordination of calcium signalling between cells is a function of the microvasculture.
endothelial cells play a key role in the regulation of hepatocyte function by coordinating Ca2+ signalling across liver tissue.
NO released by endothelial cells is a critical factor for the coordination of intercellular Ca(2+) signalling in liver.
